resources.string: Android blocks traffic if the VPN drops

After a crash, Android only lets an app start its protection again from an exact alarm, and exact alarms need Alarms & reminders access. CoreLock sets that alarm only after a crash, never while protection runs, so it does not wake your phone otherwise. Without it you get a “Protection stopped” notification instead.

Deletes your activity history, what CoreLock learned about apps and networks, alerts, HTTPS inspection content, camera and microphone events, saved recordings and exports. Your settings, rules and blocklists stay.

Sends your TCP connections through two SOCKS5 servers, so sites see server 2’s address instead of yours. SOCKS5 is not encrypted: server 1 can see your IP, every destination and your server 2 login. The content of HTTPS connections stays encrypted. SOCKS5 carries TCP only; see below for what that means.

Through the chain (You → Hop 1 → Hop 2 → Internet): every TCP connection, and your DNS lookups when DoH (encrypted DNS) is on.\nNot through the chain: plain DNS when DoH is off goes straight to your resolver, so turn on DoH. QUIC (UDP port 443) is always blocked while Dual VPN is on, so apps fall back to TCP through the chain. Other UDP (calls, games, video chat) goes direct, unless you turn on the switch below.
Strict mode (%1$s) bypasses the blocklist and is blocked; set Private DNS to Off or Automatic
Automatic: falls back to filtered DNS

Minimal blocks malware and phishing hosts only. Ads and trackers load, except the ad-SDK servers that “Block ad and attribution SDKs” in “Why am I seeing this ad?” blocks (on by default). Your own rules always apply.
Standard blocks malware, ads and trackers. At every level, your own rules apply, and so does “Block ad and attribution SDKs” in “Why am I seeing this ad?” when it is on.

Strict also blocks system telemetry (Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Mozilla, Dropbox). Some features may stop working. At every level, your own rules apply, and so does “Block ad and attribution SDKs” in “Why am I seeing this ad?” when it is on.

Background use is set to Restricted, so Android can stop protection when CoreLock is not on screen. Open battery settings and choose Unrestricted.
Battery optimization is on (the Android default). Some phones stop protection in the background anyway; if protection keeps turning off, set CoreLock\'s battery use to Unrestricted.
Unrestricted: Android will not stop CoreLock to save battery.
